raw_response:
I am 50 years old and have farmed this land for 30 years. I have no schooling, but I know my fields. With only my wife and me, I cannot tend too much labor-intensive crop, so most of my 10.9 mu stays in the wheat-maize rotation that has always fed us and given us grain to sell. The well is reliable, and I irrigate when the crops need it. I buy hybrid seed for maize and the vegetables because the yield pays for itself, and improved wheat seed because it is sturdy. I fertilize the way I have learned: compound fertilizer and urea for the grains, and heavier feeding for the vegetables because they are greedy crops. I till the vegetable plots with the rotary tiller in spring to make a soft bed, but for maize after wheat I plant directly—saves diesel and time. I spray pesticides when I see aphids, worms, or disease; the vegetables need more sprays because the insects love them. This year, I will keep about 8 mu for wheat then maize, and use the rest for tomatoes, eggplant, and watermelon to bring cash.
